notes.title: Your 동네
notes.text: Seoul is a city of neighborhoods (동네), each with its own market, pharmacies, cafés and corner stores. Most daily errands are a short walk away.

notes.title: 에 or 에서?
notes.text: Use 에 for where something IS or where you GO (시장에 있어요, 시장에 가요). Use 에서 for where you DO something (시장에서 사요).

notes.text: 저기요 ("over there…") is the polite way to get a stranger's attention: asking directions, calling a waiter, or stopping someone who dropped something.

notes.title: Asking the way
notes.text: Koreans give directions by landmarks more than street names: "go past the bank, left at the pharmacy." Subway exits are numbered, and meeting "at exit 2" (2번 출구) is very common.

notes.title: The Han River
notes.text: The Han River (한강) cuts Seoul into north and south. Its riverside parks are where Seoulites picnic, bike, order fried chicken and watch the bridges light up at night.
